csvHelp.trigger: How to get my bank data?
csvHelp.heading: Three simple steps

steps.title: Log into your bank
steps.body: Go to your bank's website or app and open your account, then go to Documents & Statements.

steps.title: Find the options
steps.body: Select the account you want — personal, business, or any account type — then click Account Statement.

steps.title: Download
steps.body: Choose the years you wish to include, then click Download, Generate, or Export. Come back here and upload it, and we'll give you clarity.

csvHelp.footer: Every major bank supports CSV export. If you run into any difficulties, ask your bank for help.

liveDemo.title:
View a real
freelance business
liveDemo.subtitle: Explore three years of Sophie Martin's freelance business. Discover how Nonodia uncovers income and expense trends, client concentration, cash flow, and forecasts.
liveDemo.ctaNote: No account required. Opens in seconds.

problem.title:
Worry less.
Nonodia gives you the answers.
problem.body: Most finance tools bury you in administrative busywork — asking: "Did you categorize this receipt?" or "Did you log this utility bill?"
problem.questionsIntro: They never answer the critical, late-night questions that actually keep independent creators awake:
questions: Is my business genuinely healthy right now?
If my current client project delays for three weeks, when do I run out of money?
How much of this invoice payment is actually mine to spend, and how much belongs to the tax collector?

valueProp.title:

items.title: Free-forever white-labeling, no "brand tax"

items.title: Live milestone runway forecasting
items.body: Milestone payments are volatile and high-ticket, not steady. We pair your monthly burn rate with your upcoming milestones, so your dashboard shows exactly how many months of runway you have — live.

items.title: The visual tax shield
items.body: See your gross payout versus your true net spendable cash instantly. Your estimated tax bracket is isolated right on your screen, so you never accidentally spend money that belongs to the tax collector.
